flawed_step: Line 0029 reverses path parity: an odd-length path starting at a red vertex ends at a blue vertex, not a red vertex.
counterexample: Let H be the 4-cycle u-v-a-b-u, colored u,a red and v,b blue. Add inside it the ear P=u-x-y-v of length 3. Alternating colors along P gives u red, x blue, y red, v blue, so the odd ear ends with the opposite color and creates no monochromatic edge, contrary to line 0029. The resulting plane graph is 2-connected, and its face-boundary lengths are 4 (u-v-y-x-u), 6 (u-x-y-v-a-b-u), and 4 (the outer cycle u-v-a-b-u), so it satisfies the problem's hypotheses.
assessment_summary: The inductive argument explicitly uses a false parity assertion about coloring an odd ear. This assertion is contradicted by a concrete graph satisfying all the stated hypotheses, so the proof is invalid as written.
